everyday_use_reason: The familiar second sense at fixed halte-là line 9 is an interjection, and current Académie A9H0116 and Larousse halte/38944 retain its figurative use to stop excessive or inappropriate words/actions. Parent halte line 57 lists this interjection derivative; derivative line 3 explicitly composes halte and là. This is an ordinary construction-bound use of frozen halte/ONO, with familiar/figurative limits, without a noun substitution, alias or exception. Robert corroborates figurative halte à, but its literal halte-là gloss is not evidence for this selected familiar sense.
selected_text_rights_reason: halte-là, fixed revision 39006229, selected familiar definition at line 9: the sentence is present in Jona’s creation revision 7379871 (2010-06-09) and corresponds to the actual DAF8 A8H0077 familiar wording, with subject/register moved into the headword/tag. Credit Académie française, eighth edition 1932–1935; the established collective original-work L123-3 boundary is 2006-01-01. Fixed wiki transcription/editorial work and Lexique adaptations/translations remain CC BY-SA 4.0 with source/history, all 17 named contributors, anonymous-history credit, modification notices and ShareAlike. The current DAF8 reference corroborates this actual origin rather than granting a later edition’s rights. Modern DAF9/Robert/Larousse editorial text, the Bazin quotation, audio and Russian translation are unselected. This verdict covers the selected text; combined packaging remains coordinator-owned.

fields.proposed_text: Ordre lancé pour faire arrêter des soldats : « Halte ! ». Le h est aspiré : muet, mais empêchant l’élision et la liaison.
fields.accepted_text: Dans l’expression familière « halte-là ! », sert à arrêter ou à faire taire quelqu’un qui dépasse les bornes.

exact_source.reviewed_excerpt: # {{familier|fr}} S’emploie lorsqu’une personne s’émancipe et va au-delà de ce qui convient, et qu’on veut l’arrêter, ou lui imposer silence.

fields.review_reason: The French definition explicitly selects familiar halte-là and retains both stopping/silencing and the person’s exceeding acceptable bounds; it does not generalise the soldiers command.
Accepted unchanged /alt/ is the parent halte interjection headword pronunciation at line 51, with h aspiré. The derivative’s /al.tə.la/ remains the construction pronunciation, not this field.

fields.proposed_text: Halt! A command to make soldiers stop. Its silent French h blocks elision and liaison (h aspiré).
fields.accepted_text: In the informal exclamation “halte-là!” (“that’s enough!”), tells someone who is overstepping acceptable bounds to stop or be quiet.

exact_source.reviewed_excerpt: # {{familier|fr}} S’emploie lorsqu’une personne s’émancipe et va au-delà de ce qui convient, et qu’on veut l’arrêter, ou lui imposer silence.

fields.review_reason: Informal exclamation and overstepping acceptable bounds render familier and va au-delà de ce qui convient; stop or be quiet preserves the two stated responses. “That’s enough!” explains this scoped rebuke.

fields.proposed_text: “立定！停止！”：让士兵停下的口令。h 不发音，但阻止省音和连诵（h aspiré）。
fields.accepted_text: 用于口语感叹语“halte-là !”（“够了！”），制止越过分寸的人，或让其住口。

exact_source.reviewed_excerpt: # {{familier|fr}} S’emploie lorsqu’une personne s’émancipe et va au-delà de ce qui convient, et qu’on veut l’arrêter, ou lui imposer silence.

fields.review_reason: 口语感叹语 marks the familiar expression, 越过分寸 retains the excessive-behaviour condition, and 制止/让其住口 retains the stopping/silencing alternatives; it is not a military order.
